entry.title: Re: SAP Joule for Consultants with SAP ECC on-prem?
entry.content:
Hi @engguygabay ,

Yes, you can potentially use SAP Joule for Consultants independently of your client's SAP ECC on-premise system.

SAP Joule for Consultants is a cloud-based SaaS application hosted on SAP BTP. It provides AI-powered assistance using SAP knowledge and documentation, helping consultants with functional questions, SAP best practices, ABAP code analysis, and implementation guidance.

The important distinction is:

  • Standalone usage: You do not necessarily need your client to upgrade from ECC to S/4HANA just to use Joule for Consultants.
  • Access requirements: You still need the appropriate commercial entitlement, SAP AI Units, SAP BTP setup, and SAP Cloud Identity Services. It is not simply a free desktop application that anyone can install.
  • ECC integration: Using Joule for Consultants as an independent consulting assistant is different from integrating Joule directly with your client's ECC system. Direct integration with ECC on-premise should not be assumed to be supported.
  • Personal access: If you are an independent consultant, check with SAP about the available commercial options for individual consultants or consulting partners. A personal SAP account alone may not be sufficient.

For your SAP HCM / HR consulting work, you can also use general-purpose AI assistants to help interpret ABAP code, understand HR infotypes and payroll concepts, troubleshoot errors, draft functional specifications, and prepare test scenarios. Always validate the answers against your ECC release, applicable SAP Notes, and client-specific configuration.

Official references:

  • SAP Joule for Consultants: https://www.sap.com/india/products/technology-platform/joule-for-consultants.html
  • SAP Help Portal – Onboarding Guide: https://help.sap.com/docs/joule/serviceguide/provisioning-sap-joule-for-consultants

entry.title: Re: Upload GL journals with 999+ line items with park/app...
entry.content:
Hi,

I looked at this in the code of my S/4HANA 2023 lab, and the workflow part also in 2020, because the answers to your first and third questions are in the Fiori posting logic itself.

1. Parking more than 999 lines without summarization: not in standard. The parked document tables keep the 3-digit item number: BUZEI is NUMC 3 in VBSEGS, VBSEGK, VBSEGD and VBSEGA, the same as in BSEG, while ACDOCA-DOCLN is CHAR 6. The BSEG bypass you found is the posting status BSTAT = 'U' ("Posting in General Ledger Only"), and CL_FDC_POSTING_IMPL refuses to park it with message FDC_POSTING_001 155 "No document parking permitted for posting status &" (foreign currency valuation is the only exception). The comment above that check says it directly: for an upload with BSTAT = 'U' but less than 999 line items, upload again with BSTAT space.

3. Workflow for a document parked with BAPI_ACC_DOCUMENT_POST: the decision is in CL_FDC_ACCDOC_VER_SERVICES, method IS_DOC_VALID_FOR_NEW_WORKFLOW. A document is relevant for the verification workflow when its transaction code is FBDC_P001 (the posting service of the Fiori apps, FAC_GL_DOCUMENT_POST_SRV), the foreign currency valuation one, or, in 2023, the supplier down payment request. Documents from the accounting interface (AWTYP BKPFF) are accepted only in the cloud edition (the check is CL_COS_UTILITIES=>IS_S4H_CLOUD). The branch for external documents on premise is in the method, commented out, with the note "this is currently not enabled", in 2020 and in 2023. On top of that the document must be parked as complete and only G/L and supplier lines are allowed (account types 'SK'). The list of the app follows the same rule: I_GLJrnlEntryToBeVerified only selects parked documents with TCODE FBDC_P001, FBDC_P050 or FBDC_P051. So a document parked by the BAPI gets a different TCODE, never shows up in Verify General Journal Entries, and no workflow starts. The released RAP business object I_JournalEntryTP (C1, ABAP Cloud) doesn't help here either: it has Post, Change, Reverse and Validate, but no park action.

2. That leaves the split. What the standard supports is several documents of up to 999 lines, each one parked and verified on its own, so the approver gets one work item per document. I didn't check whether the upload of Verify General Journal Entries has an extension point to do the split for you, so I can't confirm that part. If one approval for the whole journal is a hard requirement, that would be your own approval step before posting with the 999+ upload, and that is custom.

What I measured: the field lengths in the DDIC, the code of the three classes and the CDS view, and the message texts. I didn't run the apps, upload a file with more than 999 lines, park through the BAPI or test Public Cloud.

entry.title: HANA Integrated LiveCache Migration using SUM Homogeneous DMO
entry.content:
Migrating SAP systems to RISE is an important step toward improving system performance, simplifying the IT landscape, and preparing for digital transformation. One of the specialized scenarios in this process is HANA Integrated LiveCache Migration using SUM Homogeneous Database Migration Option (DMO), which involves migrating an SAP system along with its integrated LiveCache components to SAP HANA while maintaining system consistency and minimizing operational disruption.

The Database Migration Option (DMO) of Software Update Manager (SUM) combines system update activities with database migration, providing a streamlined approach to moving an SAP system from a supported source database to SAP HANA. In scenarios involving SAP APO or other applications that use LiveCache functionality, additional planning and technical considerations are required to ensure that LiveCache objects, data, and dependencies are handled correctly during the migration.

This blog explores the key concepts, prerequisites, preparation activities, migration approach, and important considerations involved in performing a HANA Integrated LiveCache Migration using Homogeneous DMO. It also highlights the areas that require special attention during execution, helping SAP Basis administrators and migration consultants better understand the process and prepare for a successful migration.

It is very important that we migrate the HANA LiveCache data successfully during migration.

Reason:

SUM will asks whether the LiveCache migration should be done Automatically (Taken care by SUM) or Manually (Taken care by consultant)

Selecting Automatically Scenario:

We used Automatically as this has many errors going forward in SUM.

Here, SUM run the report /SAPAPO/OM_LC_DOWNLOAD_UPLOAD at preprocessing phase just before entering the downtime (After Preparation for Downtime phase)

This report performs the consistency check and download the report. The consistency check should be passed and the download of LiveCache data takes place, this should be successful otherwise SUM will throw the error and would not be able to move forward.

And if we successfully pass the download LiveCache data in pre processing. The SUM will again try to Upload the downloaded LiveCache data in Postprocessing phase.

This will end up with an error as the report will run the consistency check in target system this will end up with error.

Note: You can skip this error by following the instruction in this SAP note 2562164.

Solution and helpful suggestion:

Choose manual execution of LiveCache report so that we can manually download and upload the LiveCache data.

You can use the new report i.e., /SAPAPO/OM_LC_DOWNLOAD_UPLOAD2

This report does not validate the consistency check of LiveCache.

During pre processing SUM will provide you the screen for downloading the LiveCache data.

Logon to the system and execute the report /SAPAPO/OM_LC_DOWNLOAD_UPLOAD2

Make sure the section A is performed and the table is empty before downloading the LiveCache data

Above image has data we are going to clear that.

Click on “Delete Download Table and Logs” to delete the previously downloaded Livecache data so that we can freshly download.

The above image is after deleting the previously downloaded data (Section A)

Now, click on “Download LiveCache Data” in section B. This will download the LiveCache data into a table.

You can see the number of entries in the table. The name of the table is /SAPAPO/OMDWNUPL (Just for validation purpose)

After this step of downloading the LiveCache data kindly proceed forward with the SUM downtime.

Now, in SUM Post Processing Phase

SUM will stop and ask to upload the downloaded live cache data on target system.

Login to the target system and execute the report /SAPAPO/OM_LC_DOWNLOAD_UPLOAD2

The screen will look something like this before upload on target.

Now, kindly select option on section C: Upload Upload LiveCacheData

After successfully uploading the LiveCache data the screen will look something like below.

Note: Please do not click anything in section A and section B. In target system we should only select section C: Upload

After this we can proceed with the SUM. This completes the successful migration of LiveCache data from source to target.

The downloaded data will be in database. We should run this report and upload the LiveCache data from the database to the HANA LiveCache and this is our responsibility.

Thank You,
Ranjith R

RISE with SAP SCM APO SAP LiveCache software logistics toolset

entry.title: Re: SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud – Are New G/L Accounts Autom...
entry.content:
Hi,

Short answer from the code: yes, a G/L account created in the system itself is added to the hierarchies whose range covers it, without editing and saving the hierarchy again. I checked it in my S/4HANA 2023 lab, which is on premise but uses the same Manage Global Hierarchies runtime, so keep the release difference in mind.

Why something has to do it: the range only exists in the design time of the hierarchy (a node with a range sign and a low and high value). The runtime that the reports read, HRRP_NODE and HRRP_NODE_N, has one leaf per account and no range field at all. In my lab the FSV hierarchies have 53,126 leaf nodes. So a new account needs its own leaf.

What does it: the G/L account master has the BAdI GL_ACCOUNT_MASTER_REPLICATE, and SAP's implementation FINS_FI_GLACC_HRRP_REPLICATION (class CL_FINS_HRRP_GLACC_REP_BADIIMP) calls function module HRRP_GL_ACCOUNT_DELTA with the chart of accounts, the account and the action. For an insert it updates the OB58 FSVs and the Manage Global Hierarchies FSVs, and then runs a generic delta (CL_FINS_UH_HRRP_DELTA_UPDATE) that looks for range nodes where the account is between the low and the high value and creates the leaf in the runtime tables. In dialog the function module runs as a background task after the save, so the account shows up a moment later, not in the same second.

About KBA 3587911: an account that arrives by transport is written by the import and doesn't go through the G/L account save, so this BAdI doesn't run for it. That is my reading of the code and it fits the KBA. The same function module also has a cloud branch: when the system is cloud and the Q2P transport is active, it transports the affected FSV and hierarchy versions after the update.

What I measured: the runtime tables, the BAdI implementation, the function module and the delta class in the 2023 lab. I didn't create an account to watch it happen, and I didn't test Public Cloud 2602 or the transport case of the KBA.

entry.title: Re: Parallel crcy area (crcy type 40) missing for area 01...
entry.content:
Hi,

You already found the cause. The long text of ACC_AA 116 says it directly: the parallel currencies of the leading ledger and the depreciation areas in Asset Accounting must be the same. Company code 830 has currency type 40 (hard currency) and 030 doesn't, so CDCN never needed an area for type 40, and the copy CD83 doesn't have one either.

That leaves two ways:

  • If 830 really needs the hard currency, add a parallel currency area for type 40 to CD83 and then assign the chart.
  • If type 40 in 830 came from the copy and nobody needs it, remove it from the currency settings of 830 instead. Decide this before the first postings in 830.

How the area should look: SAP's sample chart 0CL in my S/4HANA 2023 lab already has one. Area 01 Book deprec. posts in real time, and area 50 "Hard curr." has currency type 40 (field CURTP in T093A), takes the values from 01 (Adoption of Values from Depreciation Area = 01), takes the depreciation terms from 01 (Dep. Terms Transfer = 01) and is set to "Area Does Not Post". That is exactly what the long text asks: the parallel currency area must have the same settings as the posting area, and the only difference is that it doesn't post. The sample charts 0AR, 0CO, 0MX, 0PE and 0VE also have type 40 areas if you want to compare.

In the IMG of Asset Accounting the steps are: Determine Depreciation Areas (create the new area in CD83, copying 01), Specify Transfer of APC Values and Specify Transfer of Depreciation Terms (both from 01), and Specify the Use of Parallel Currencies (type 40 for the new area). Then try the assignment of CD83 to 830 again.

What I measured: the message and its long text, T093 and T093A of the sample charts, and the names of the IMG activities, all in my S/4HANA 2023 lab. I didn't build the area in a chart and assign it to a company code, so try it in a sandbox first.

entry.title: How to enable CDS CDC extraction on S/4HANA table VBFA with RUUID (RAW16) primary key?
entry.content:
Hi Community,

I am trying to build a custom CDS extraction view on table VBFA (Sales Document Flow) in SAP S/4HANA 2025 to replicate data via ODP / Change Data Capture (CDC) into an external analytical target ( BW/4HANA embedded in SAP S/4HANA).

Due to the S/4HANA table restructuring of VBFA, the physical primary key in DDIC is:

  • MANDT

  • RUUID (Data Type: RAW(16))

The legacy functional business keys (VBELV, POSNV, VBELN, POSNN, VBTYP_N) are now regular non-key columns.

Approaches Attempted & Errors

0. automatic change data capture annotation => Fail

1. Manual CDC Mapping on Business Keys When attempting to define @analytics.dataExtraction.delta.changeDataCapture.mapping using the business fields:

 
@Analytics.dataExtraction.delta.changeDataCapture.mapping: [{ 
   table: 'VBFA',
   role : #MAIN,
   tableElement: [ 'VBELV', 'VBELN', 'POSNV', 'POSNN', 'VBTYP_N' ],
   viewElement:  [ 'vbelv', 'vbeln', 'posnv', 'posnn', 'vbtyp_n' ]
}]

  • Result: Activation fails immediately with:

    • Error while reading CDC annotations: mapping field does not exist [Analytics]

    • Error while reading CDC annotations: No #MAIN table specified [Analytics](The compiler rejects them because they are not physical primary key fields in table VBFA).

2. Using RUUID as Key with Automatic CDC If I define ruuid as the sole view entity key and set delta.changeDataCapture.automatic: true:

 
define view entity ZBQR_CDS_VBFA as select from vbfa {
  key ruuid,
      vbelv,
      posnv,
      vbeln,
      posnn,
      vbtyp_n,
      ...
}

  • Result: While it can compile, RAW(16) creates severe compatibility issues during replication. The consumer/target does not accept raw binary fields as unique keys for the ADSO, and converting it via bintohex(ruuid) cannot be used as an underlying table key for CDC database triggers.

3. Using @analytics.dataExtraction.alternativeKey I tried specifying the functional fields via @analytics.dataExtraction.alternativeKey as documented for (ABAP 8.16) while retaining key ruuid:

 
@Analytics.dataExtraction: {
  enabled: true,

      vbelv,
      posnv,
      vbeln,
      posnn,
      vbtyp_n,
      ...
}

  • Result: same error as (1).

 

Another fact:

For the same approaches with MATDOC table the CDS view works correctly with RODPS_REPL_TEST delta extraction using BINTOHEX conversion.

VBFA do not pass RODPS_REPL_TEST delta extraction in any case.

My Questions:

  2. How should @analytics.dataExtraction.alternativeKey be correctly configured in conjunction with trigger-based CDC?

  3. Is trigger-based CDS CDC supported on VBFA, or is it required to fall back to a date/timestamp-based delta (or SLT)?

Thank you in advance for your support!

entry.title: Re: File attachments at header level of requisitions
entry.content:
Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Here is the AI-generated response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

Header Attachments for Purchase Requisitions via Workflow

Header attachments are supported for purchase requisitions in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, but support depends on the application, release, attachment framework, and point in the process. Header attachment enablement was delivered for Public Edition in release 2302 through the attachment facet.[1] However, the My Purchase Requisitions app still supports attachment creation only at item level.[2]

Workflow limitation

Standard flexible workflow does not provide an activity for an approver to upload a new attachment to the purchase requisition header during approval. The workflow inbox primarily displays attachments already linked to the business object. Therefore, calling API_CV_ATTACHMENT_SRV from workflow custom logic should not be treated as a supported method unless the API metadata for your tenant explicitly exposes the purchase-requisition header as a supported business object and permits creation.

This is distinct from private-edition functionality: from SAP S/4HANA 2025, My Inbox can display existing purchase-requisition header attachments, but that feature applies to SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, not Public Edition.[3]

Standard options

  1. Add the attachment before workflow submission

    • Use Manage Purchase Requisitions – Professional or Create Purchase Requisition – Advanced, depending on the process and release.
    • For newer releases supporting header DMS attachments, add the document through the header Documents/Attachment area rather than the GOS-style attachment list.
    • In release 2602, external DMS document type SL1 can be added at PR header level and can subsequently flow to the purchase order.[4]

  2. Configure Harmonized Document Management

    • In configuration activity/SSCUI 105346 – Activate HDM for Attachment Object Type, activate:
      • PURCHASEREQUISITION
      • PURCHASEREQUISITIONITEM
      • PURCHASEORDER, if PR-to-PO transfer is required.
    • Activate the DMS framework and maintain the applicable default document type:
      • SL1 – external use
      • SL9 – internal use.[4]
    • Ensure the business role contains authorization to change PR attachments; the relevant standard catalogs include SAP_MM_BC_PR_PROCESS_MC and SAP_MM_BC_SSPPR_MANAGE_PC.

  3. Use item-level attachments where self-service requisitioning is required

    • Item-level attachments remain the standard supported approach in My Purchase Requisitions.[2]
    • This is generally the safest option when approvers must see documents associated with individual approval items.

  4. Side-by-side extension

    • If the attachment must be collected during approval, implement a separate SAP Build Process Automation or SAP BTP application to collect and store the document.
    • Link it to the PR through a supported released API only after confirming that the target release exposes header-level attachment creation for the PR object.
    • Do not rely on an undocumented business-object type or internal object key with API_CV_ATTACHMENT_SRV, because this is not a stable, supported Public Cloud extension pattern.
Important distinction

GOS and DMS attachments behave differently. GOS attachments are assigned to one business object and are not transferred automatically from PR header to PO header; SAP supports item-level transfer when both objects use DMS attachments.[5] For release 2602, the supported header transfer path uses DMS/HDM and requires documents to be uploaded in the header Documents area, not through the GOS attachment list.[4]

Recommendation: If your tenant is on 2602 or later, use the standard HDM/DMS header configuration and require the requester or purchaser to attach the document before submitting the PR. If your release or application does not expose that header capability, use item-level attachments or a side-by-side document-collection process. Adding a PR header attachment directly from an approval step is not a standard flexible-workflow capability.

Batch Printing Correspondence

No. Standard batch printing is not supported directly from Manage Journal Entries or Manage Supplier Line Items. Manage Journal Entries only navigates to Create Correspondence, where correspondence is created for an individual document.[1]

For journal entries, use Create Correspondence (F0744A) with correspondence type SAP09 Internal Document and select either Entry View or Ledger View. If the requirement is to print accounting documents by document range, evaluate Accounting Document Output together with Maintain Print Queues and SAP Cloud Print Manager. SAP guidance describes selecting parameters in Accounting Document Output and sending the resulting documents through a configured print queue.[4] SAP Cloud Print Manager is required for unattended or automatic mass printing.[5]

For supplier-invoice correspondence, the standard process may remain document-specific; for example, complaint-letter output is opened and printed from an individual supplier invoice.[6] If no suitable mass-output app exists for the required correspondence type, consider a side-by-side extension using released APIs, or submit a feature request through SAP Customer Influence.[1]

SAP S/4HANA Cloud: Mass Update BP SSF Communication Type

Use the full BusinessPartnerTemplate generated by your tenant, not the example file. Example files are illustrative and may omit optional fields; the full template contains all fields supported by the current system. The import app can generate either an example file or a full system-specific template.[1]

For the SSF column:

  • Enter X to activate SSF as the business partner’s communication type.
  • Leave it blank if SSF should not be selected.
  • Do not enter the text SSF.
  • Retain the BP key and all mandatory technical/key columns from the generated template.

For existing business partners:

  1. Export the affected records with Export Master Data – Business Partners.
  2. Keep the exported structure unchanged and populate SSF with X.
  3. Upload it using Import Master Data – Business Partners (F6553A, successor to the former Import Data for Consolidation app).[2]
  4. Run the consolidation process and validate a small test set before processing all BPs.

If the SSF value represents a new subordinate record rather than an update to an existing BP record, unhide _ACTION_CODE and enter uppercase I. SAP specifies that new rows are inserted through file upload using an action code; updates to existing values normally do not require it.[3] [4]

If SSF = X is rejected during validation, do not try alternate values blindly. Confirm the field tooltip/value help in the generated template and raise an SAP support incident for the BP mass-processing component, because field availability and accepted operations can vary by release.

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud: Recurring Journal Entries at Scale

A supported standard mass-creation option for recurring journal entry templates does not currently exist in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. SAP confirms that F1598 has no mass-upload function and that no API is available for creating recurring journal entries in bulk.[1] An Excel upload for recurring templates is likewise unavailable.[2]

A. Mass creation of recurring journal entries
  • F1598 supports creating and saving individual recurring entries, including their line items and recurrence rules.[3]
  • The recurring entry is only a template; scheduled processing later creates the actual journal entries.[4]
  • There is no supported bulk-create mechanism for these templates in Public Edition.[1]
  • Do not build against FAC_RECURRING_ACCOUNTING_DOC_SRV unless SAP explicitly lists and releases it for your Public Edition release. The technical information available for that service identifies support for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition rather than Public Edition.[4]
B. Mass upload of recurring templates

There is no standard spreadsheet, CSV, migration object, or released interface for uploading recurring-entry templates in Public Edition.[1] [2]

The Upload General Journal Entries app, F2548, can import multiple ordinary journal entries from XLSX or CSV and post them, but it uploads actual general journal entries—not recurring templates or recurrence rules.[5] [6]

C. Supported alternatives

  1. Upload each period’s actual journals with F2548

    Generate the period’s journal-entry file externally and upload it through F2548. The app supports multiple entries per file, error correction using the original batch ID, verification, and posting.[5]

    This is generally appropriate when:

    • periodic amounts or account assignments can change;
    • business users want spreadsheet-based control;
    • the volume is manageable as a controlled file upload.

  2. Post actual journals through the released Journal Entry API

    For high-volume or unattended processing, generate each period’s due postings outside the recurring-template framework and send them through a released Journal Entry Post API. SAP identifies synchronous and asynchronous bulk SOAP interfaces for remote journal posting, with the bulk interface intended for larger workloads.[7] SAP guidance also identifies journal-entry APIs as suitable for large transaction volumes.[8]

    This automates actual journal creation, not creation of F1598 recurring templates.

  3. Use a clean-core side-by-side solution on SAP BTP

    A scalable pattern is to maintain schedules and template data in a side-by-side application, calculate the due postings, validate accounting objects, and call only released SAP APIs. Similar implementations use SAP Integration Suite for inbound orchestration and SAP BTP for mappings, transformations, and posting generation.[9] [10] This approach supports tailored business rules without compromising SAP S/4HANA upgrade stability.

  4. Assess process-specific automation

    If the entries represent accruals, deferrals, allocations, leases, or another defined accounting process, assess the relevant standard process automation rather than reproducing everything as generic recurring journals. F1598 is most suitable where posting keys, accounts, and amounts remain fixed.[4]

D. Recommended scalable approach

Use the following decision model:

  • Small, stable template population: Create templates manually in F1598, use copy where practical, and run the standard recurring-posting process.
  • Large population with periodic file preparation: Generate actual postings externally and use F2548.
  • Large, repeatable, unattended volume: Store schedules outside F1598, generate due journals on SAP BTP or another governed integration layer, and post through a released journal-entry API.
  • One-time opening balance or cutover requirement: Use the applicable migration object for balances or open items, not recurring-template migration. Migration and operational journal posting are separate use cases.[8]

For the BTP/API option, include:

  1. A governed schedule and template store.
  2. Company-code, currency, account-assignment, and balancing validations.
  3. Idempotency keys to prevent duplicate postings.
  4. Simulation or approval before posting where required.
  5. Batching and API payload-size controls.
  6. Error staging, correction, and reprocessing.
  7. Posting-result reconciliation and audit logging.
  8. Monitoring and notifications for failed runs.
Conclusion

Your assessment is correct: F1598 cannot mass-upload recurring journal entry templates in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and there is currently no released recurring-entry creation API for that purpose.[1] The supported scalable alternative is to automate the resulting periodic journal entries through F2548 or a released Journal Entry Post API, preferably using a clean-core SAP BTP side-by-side design for high-volume requirements.[5] [7] If native recurring-template mass creation remains mandatory, the appropriate route is to support the published SAP feature request referenced in the relevant SAP KBA.[1]

Standard SES Supplier Notification in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608

No. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 does not provide standard output functionality that automatically sends an approved Service Entry Sheet (SES) to the supplier by email or generates a printable SES PDF.

  • Supplier notification: Flexible Workflow supports configurable approval-result emails containing details such as the decision reason and referenced purchase order.[1] These workflow notifications are intended for workflow participants, such as approvers and the SES creator, rather than the supplier.
  • SES output: The standard Manage Service Entry Sheets app does not offer output-message functionality.[2]
  • PDF: Standard SES printout/output is not available; SAP indicates that SES output is generated only when converted to a purchase order.[3]
  • Approval process: Flexible Workflow remains the standard mechanism for automatic, one-step, or multistep SES approval in this release.[4]

Therefore, the requirement to email SES details to the supplier after approval—especially with a PDF attachment—requires a clean-core extension or integration. A suitable design is to react to the approved SES status, retrieve the required SES and supplier-contact data through released interfaces, generate a PDF if required, and send the email through an approved communication service. The implementation should include recipient determination, duplicate-prevention logic, monitoring, authorization controls, and error handling.

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Kind regards,

Henrike

Troubleshooting: Credit Memo Tax Dates

This behavior is generally standard because SAP treats a credit memo as a correction invoice rather than as a normal invoice.

  • Credit memo with reference to an original invoice: The Tax Fulfilment Date is derived from the original invoice’s Tax Fulfilment Date. The Tax Reporting Date is normally derived from the credit memo’s billing date. Therefore, the Service Rendered Date entered in VF01 is not necessarily used.[1]
  • Credit memo without reference: The Tax Fulfilment Date is derived from the Service Rendered Date, while the Tax Reporting Date follows the correction-invoice rule and is normally the credit memo billing date.[1]
  • For normal invoices, the Tax Fulfilment Date is generally the Service Rendered Date and the Tax Reporting Date equals the Tax Fulfilment Date, which explains the different result you observe.[1]
  • The SD-to-FI transfer executes user exit EXIT_SAPLV60B_008 to determine these two tax dates.
Can the VF01 Service Rendered Date be transferred?

Yes, but the appropriate method depends on the deployment and country localization:

  1. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition for Poland
    Use configuration activity Transfer VAT Date from Credit Memo to Journal Entry (SSCUI 105418). It permits selection of either the Service Rendered Date or Billing Date as the VAT date.[2]

  2. On-premise or private-edition systems
    Review the implementation of EXIT_SAPLV60B_008. SAP provides sample logic in SAP Note 3004838; any adjustment must comply with the applicable country-specific tax rules.[1]

  3. FI VAT-date framework
    Check whether VAT-date functionality is active for the company code and review enhancement spot VATDATE_RULES, BAdI VATDATE_VALUES, and the relevant implementation. This framework determines and validates BKPF-VATDATE, including documents originating from VF01.[3]

Recommended checks
  1. Determine whether the credit memo references the original invoice.
  2. Compare the original invoice’s Tax Fulfilment Date with the credit memo’s resulting date.
  3. Verify the credit memo billing type and copy-control path used for its creation; credit memos can follow separate source-document and transfer logic.[4]
  4. Debug EXIT_SAPLV60B_008 during release to accounting and check whether localization or custom code overwrites the VF01 Service Rendered Date.[1]
  5. Confirm the required date logic with the local tax team before changing it, because the standard correction-invoice behavior reflects legal reporting rules.

entry.title: Re: Group Reporting: scheduled Goodwill amortization
entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question.

Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

SAP Group Reporting: HGB Goodwill Amortization

Yes. A workaround exists in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, and SAP Asset Accounting is generally not the appropriate mechanism for it.

SAP’s recommended Group Reporting approach is:

  1. Use activity-based consolidation of investments with goodwill in local currency.
  2. Post the amortization amount to the statistical FS item $GW_IMP for each amortization period.
  3. Let the consolidation-of-investments task generate the corresponding goodwill reduction and expense postings.
  4. To avoid entering $GW_IMP manually every period, implement the reclassification-task approach described in the attachment GW_scheduled_amortization.pdf to SAP Note 2813262. SAP states that this approach is usable from release OP2025 and that Public Cloud systems receive all applicable features.[1]

Public Edition already supports goodwill calculation in local currency and subsequent currency-translation-reserve adjustments.[2] Manual impairment adjustments are supported for the goodwill-in-local-currency methods, with the subsequent consolidation postings generated by activity-based consolidation of investments.[3]

Asset Accounting should not be used as the primary solution because consolidated goodwill is Group Reporting data rather than an operational fixed asset. Routing it through Asset Accounting would introduce unnecessary accounting-to-consolidation mappings, ledger considerations, and reconciliation requirements. It could also mix legal-entity depreciation with a group-level consolidation adjustment.

The practical design is therefore to keep the process entirely within Group Reporting:

  • Store the amortization basis and useful-life logic in dedicated statistical FS items.
  • Use reclassification rules to calculate or supply the periodic $GW_IMP amount.
  • Run the reclassification before the activity-based consolidation-of-investments task.
  • Add validation rules to prevent amortization beyond the remaining goodwill balance.
  • Test acquisition-year prorating, subsequent capitalization, ownership changes, disposals, currency translation, reversals, and balance carryforward.

For rule-based consolidation of investments, goodwill itself is manually calculated and posted because the underlying records do not contain the required parent partner unit.[4] If this is your current method, assess whether activity-based consolidation with goodwill in local currency is a better foundation for the HGB process.

entry.content:
#AI-Generated Content

Hello,

Thank you very much for your question. Our internal AI tool has provided the following response. Please check whether it helps you resolve the issue.

Kind regards,

Henrike

 

Standard SAP Approach for Hong Kong Tax Depreciation

Use SAP Asset Accounting with a separate tax depreciation area for Hong Kong tax values, while retaining the normal book depreciation area for financial accounting. Depreciation areas support parallel book and tax valuations, and multiple Hong Kong company codes can share one country-specific chart of depreciation where their requirements are identical.[1]

Recommended design

  • Book and tax valuations: Keep book depreciation in the posting area and calculate Hong Kong capital allowances in a separate, normally non-posting tax area. Tax areas are intended for statutory tax reporting and book-to-tax reconciliation.[2]

  • Asset classification: Create distinct asset classes for:

    • Industrial buildings
    • Commercial buildings
    • Plant and machinery pool at 10%
    • Plant and machinery pool at 20%
    • Plant and machinery pool at 30%

    Asset classes should default the relevant tax treatment and account determination. Each asset must still be represented individually for operational control and disposal processing.

  • Industrial buildings: Request a tax depreciation key that combines a 20% first-year allowance with a 4% annual allowance.

  • Commercial buildings: Use or request a tax depreciation key providing the 4% annual allowance, subject to the required year-of-acquisition convention.

  • Plant and machinery: Request three reducing-balance tax keys for 10%, 20%, and 30%, each incorporating the 60% initial allowance in the acquisition year. Assign assets to the appropriate rate class or pool through asset class defaults.

Public Edition configuration limits

Customer-created depreciation keys are not generally available directly in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. From release 2402, new pre-approved custom depreciation keys can be requested through Expert Configuration by submitting an incident for the development system and completing SAP’s depreciation-key template; the customer must test the keys before production deployment.[3]

Additional depreciation areas are supported through scope item 5HG – Asset Accounting – Additional Depreciation Area, but this must be selected during initial scoping and cannot normally be added afterward.[3] If the required tax area was not activated initially, confirm available expert-configuration options with SAP before finalizing the design.

After changing an asset’s value, depreciation method, or useful life, use the Schedule Asset Accounting Jobs app with the Recalculate Depreciation template.[4]

Pool and disposal treatment

The depreciation engine can calculate asset-level initial and annual allowances, but the Hong Kong plant-and-machinery rules require pool-level written-down-value calculations and disposal proceeds to reduce the pool rather than necessarily producing an asset-level balancing result. Standard group-asset functionality should not be selected as the long-term design because it is compatibility-scope functionality; SAP identifies individual assets with common depreciation parameters and grouped reporting fields as an alternative.[5]

Therefore:

  1. Post each acquisition and retirement against the individual fixed asset.
  2. Capture disposal proceeds through standard retirement transactions.
  3. Aggregate acquisition cost, allowances, and proceeds by company code, tax year, and 10%/20%/30% pool.
  4. Calculate pool-level written-down values, balancing charges, statutory caps, and cessation adjustments in a tax reconciliation layer.
  5. Post any required tax adjustment separately or retain it as a statistical tax-reporting adjustment, depending on the agreed accounting design.

For buildings, standard retirement processing can supply cost, accumulated tax depreciation, and proceeds, but the statutory balancing allowance or charge and its cap should be validated in the tax calculation. For plant and machinery, a released custom analytical report, side-by-side extension, or controlled spreadsheet/tax application will normally be required for pool roll-forward, disposal offsets, balancing-charge caps, and cessation-of-business calculations.

Conclusion

The standard-fit approach is parallel tax valuation plus dedicated asset classes and SAP-approved depreciation keys. The initial and annual allowance calculations can largely reside in Asset Accounting. The Hong Kong pool-level disposal and balancing logic is the main functional gap and should be handled through a controlled tax-calculation extension and reconciliation, rather than through unsupported core modification. Before build, obtain confirmation from local tax advisers and submit the exact calculation examples to SAP through an incident; SAP recommends raising an incident where delivered depreciation keys do not meet a mandatory localization requirement.[6]

SAP DMS Attachment Inheritance Across Versions

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, creating a new Document Info Record version copies the existing originals by standard design. There is no standard configuration to prevent Version 0 attachments from being inherited by Version 1.[1]

To meet the requirement:

  1. In the Manage Documents app, choose Create New Version to create Version 1; Check-in as New Version creates a new attachment version rather than a new Document Info Record version.[2]
  2. Open the Originals/Attachments section of Version 1.
  3. Remove the copied Version 0 attachment.
  4. Upload the new attachment and save Version 1.

Removing the attachment from Version 1 does not remove it from Version 0 because each DIR version is maintained separately. SAP supports deleting attachments from the attachment area and saving the change.[3]

Therefore, the requirement cannot be automated through standard configuration in Public Edition. The supported standard approach is to remove the inherited original manually from Version 1 and then upload the replacement.[1]

entry.title: Re: Can we automate this entire calculation sequence and...
entry.content:
Hi,

I looked at what the standard has for each part in my S/4HANA 2023 lab.

1. On premise and in private edition, yes, the Advance Return (RFUMSV00) can post the balance itself. Its selection screen has a block for the tax payable posting: "Batch Input Session Required" (PAR_BINP), session name, document type, posting date and period, due date, an alternative tax payable account (PAR_ZKTO), and options to process the session right away or keep it. With the flag set, the report keeps the tax payable balances of the run and creates a batch input session with the transfer posting, so nobody types the amount.

2. If your VAT return runs in Advanced Compliance Reporting, ACR has its own tax payable posting (activity TAX_PAYABLE_POSTING), and SAP released a BAdI on it: SRF_MOD_TAX_PAYABLE_POSTING (enhancement spot ES_SRF_TAX_PAYABLE_POSTING, C1, released for key user and cloud). The method MODIFY_TAX_PAYABLE_POSTING receives the reporting entity, category, run ID and report ID, the reported items (document, tax code, G/L account, tax amounts) and the lines of the posting (company code, G/L account, balance), and can change those lines and the posting date. Check first if your return really runs in ACR: in my lab the only China categories are "China Construct Input VAT" and "China Transfer Input VAT".

3. Post Tax Payables runs on FAC_TAX_PAYABLE_POST_SRV, a generic posting service (it inherits from CL_FAC_FINANCIALS_POST_DPC_EXT). I didn't find a released API for that app. For an automated posting I would use the released journal entry API, I_JournalEntryTP (C1 in my lab).

4. For the surtax accrual base I didn't find a standard calculation. What I would build is a periodic job that reads the balances of the accounts in your formula after the VAT and consumption tax postings, with the released views I_GLAccountLineItem or I_JournalEntryItem (both C1), calculates the base and posts the accrual through I_JournalEntryTP. If all the components come out of the ACR run, the BAdI from point 2 is the other place to do it.

What I measured: the RFUMSV00 source and selection texts, the BAdI interface and its release state, the ACR report categories and the release state of the views and the API, all in the 2023 lab. I didn't run RFUMSV00 with batch input, an ACR posting or the BAdI, and I didn't test Public Cloud or the China localization.

entry.title: Re: ATP for Production Orders Creation
entry.content:
HI

Please check the checking rule maintained in OPJK for Availability Check during Creation (Rule 1).

The checking rule used during Production Order Creation (1) and Production Order Release (2) should be the same. If different checking rules are assigned, the system may use different settings in OPJJ (Availability Check Control), which can result in different ATP outcomes during order creation and release.

Note: Availability Check results are determined by the combination of:

  • Checking Rule (maintained in OPJK)
  • Checking Group (maintained in the Material Master → MRP 3 view)

Since the same material is being checked during both creation and release, the Checking Group remains unchanged. Therefore, the most likely cause of differing ATP results is a difference in the Checking Rule being applied.

Please ensure that the same checking rule is maintained for both Creation (1) and Release (2) so that the system follows the same availability check logic in both scenarios.

entry.title: Re: How to Connect Claude Code to ABAP with Zero-Config MCP
entry.content:
@eswar_gajjala66 , Thanks for reading the blog.

Hi, this error SEDI_ADT_PROGRAM deserialization failure is a known ADT issue that typically occurs on BTP trial systems when trying to create certain ABAP object types programmatically via the ADT API.

The BTP free trial ABAP environment (Steampunk) has restrictions on which object types can be created via ADT API calls, particularly executable programs using the classic REPORT syntax. Steampunk is an ABAP Cloud environment which means it enforces strict ABAP Cloud rules, classic program types are not supported, only Cloud-compliant object types.

One way to fix is change what you are asking Claude to create:Instead of asking Claude to create a classic executable program, ask it to create a class-based ABAP Cloud compliant object:

 
Create an ABAP class ZCL_DEMO_REPORT in package 
ZLOCAL using ABAP Cloud syntax. No classic REPORT 
statement. Use CL_SALV_TABLE for output if needed. 
This is a Steampunk BTP trial environment.

Or alternatively - create a RAP Business Object instead:

Steampunk is purpose-built for RAP development. Claude Code + MCP works very well for RAP BO generation on BTP trial systems, stick to that object type and you will not hit this error.

One more thing to check:

Make sure your package is ZLOCAL ,on BTP trial this is the correct local package. Using $TMP or custom packages can sometimes trigger serialization issues on Steampunk systems.

Hope that resolves it!

entry.title: Anomaly Detection with AI in SAP Cloud ALM for Operations
entry.content:
Introduction

Static thresholds are the weak spot of most monitoring setups. Set them too tight and operations teams drown in alerts. Set them too loose and a real problem slips through until a user calls the service desk. And a value that is perfectly normal on a Monday morning can be a warning sign on a Sunday night.

SAP Cloud ALM for Operations now addresses this with a set of AI capabilities that learn what "normal" looks like for your landscape and flag deviations from it. In this post I give an overview of these capabilities, explain how they fit together from detection to resolution, and share practical tips from customer projects on getting started.

What SAP Cloud ALM offers today

The AI capabilities are not a separate product. They are built into the existing monitoring use cases and fall into three groups: detecting anomalies, recommending thresholds, and helping to resolve alerts.

Use caseCapabilityWhat it does

Health Monitoring

Dynamic Thresholds

Calculates thresholds automatically from historical data and trend analysis, so the system learns the normal behavior of a metric and flags deviations.

Real User Monitoring

Change point detection and seasonal anomaly suppression

Detects significant changes in user-facing performance. Alerts caused by predictable patterns, such as weekly peaks or quarter-end spikes, can be suppressed.

Integration & Exception Monitoring

Anomaly detection on message volume

The event "Anomaly Detected in the Number of Messages Processed" fires when a business service processes more or fewer messages than expected within a time period.

Integration & Exception Monitoring

AI-recommended thresholds

Uses machine learning on historical message counts to suggest threshold values, shown with a trend chart of past volumes.

Business Process Monitoring

AI threshold recommendations

Analyzes the last seven days of document volumes and suggests KPI event thresholds for review.

Alert Management

ALM Alert Resolution Agent

Analyzes alert details, error messages, thresholds and system context, searches documentation, KBAs and SAP Notes, and suggests troubleshooting steps on the Alert Details page.

Dashboards

ALM Dashboard Generation Agent

Creates dashboard cards from system and service data using natural-language prompts.

 

In Health Monitoring, the Quality column shows how far each metric's model has come:

  • Predictive: the model is actively generating thresholds.
  • Learning: more data is being collected.
  • Static: the metric behaves too constantly for a reliable prediction.
  • Insufficient: there is not enough suitable data for predictive modeling.

SAP positions these features as steps toward "Autonomous ALM": from dynamic thresholds and change point detection today toward continuous detection of critical situations, guided resolution with Joule and, eventually, automated remediation.

How it works

 

The monitoring use cases collect the data, the AI layer learns what is normal and flags deviations, and Alert Management routes the result to the right team. The Alert Resolution Agent then supports the first analysis, so the team starts with context instead of a bare alert.

Getting started

The AI capabilities build on a working monitoring setup. If data is already flowing into SAP Cloud ALM, you can start in a few steps:

  1. Connect your systems and services. Anomaly detection needs history, so the earlier data collection starts, the sooner the models have something to learn from.
  2. Activate the monitoring use cases you want to use: Health Monitoring, Real User Monitoring, Integration & Exception Monitoring or Business Process Monitoring.
  3. Switch selected metrics to dynamic thresholds in Health Monitoring, and check the Quality column until they reach "Predictive".
  4. Use "Recommend" for anomaly events in Integration & Exception Monitoring. Review the suggested values against the trend chart, apply them, and regenerate them when the behavior of the monitored service changes.
  5. Accept or adjust the KPI threshold recommendations in Business Process Monitoring.
  6. Route the resulting alerts through Alert Management and Intelligent Event Processing to the right teams via email, Microsoft Teams or your ITSM tool.
  7. Use the ALM Alert Resolution Agent on the Alert Details page to speed up the first analysis.

Lessons from customer projects

  • Start where the noise is. Begin with the metrics and interfaces that generate the most false alerts today. That is where dynamic thresholds pay off fastest and win the trust of the operations team.
  • Give the models time. A metric in "Learning" or "Insufficient" state is not a configuration error. Keep static thresholds in place for critical metrics until the model is predictive.
  • Treat recommendations as a starting point. AI-recommended thresholds are based on past behavior. If the past contains an incident, review the values before you apply them.
  • Decide who gets which alert before go-live. Detection is only half the job. Agree with the Basis, integration and application teams which alerts go to whom and through which channel.
  • Mind the scope for non-SAP systems. Anomaly detection works on the data that reaches SAP Cloud ALM. Third-party systems need to be connected first, for example via OpenTelemetry.

entry.title: Monitoring Dashboards in SAP Cloud ALM for Operations
entry.content:
Introduction

SAP Cloud ALM for Operations collects data from many monitoring use cases, each in its own app. But most people start their day with one question: is everything running, and if not, where do I need to look?

The Monitoring Dashboards app answers that question on a single page. This post shows the predefined dashboards, how to build your own, and how Joule creates dashboard cards from a prompt.

Dashboard options in SAP Cloud ALM

The Monitoring Dashboards app comes with predefined pages and lets you build your own on top of them.

DashboardTypeWhat it shows

Operational Status

Predefined

The status of applications, jobs and integrations in one place

Services Status

Predefined

Service status based on Health Monitoring, Real User Monitoring and Integration & Exception Monitoring

Chart Examples

Predefined

The available chart types, as a reference for your own cards

Personalized dashboard

Custom

Cards from a predefined card library, combining analytics from all Operations apps

Predefined pages cannot be edited directly. To customize one, duplicate it and edit the copy.

Besides the Monitoring Dashboards app, each monitoring use case has its own embedded analytics, without extra configuration. For reporting outside SAP Cloud ALM, the data can be consumed in SAP Analytics Cloud, Grafana or any tool that uses the Analytics API or the OpenTelemetry-based Raw Data Outbound APIs.

How it fits together

The monitoring use cases deliver the data, the Monitoring Dashboards app turns it into pages for each audience, and the same data can also flow to external analytics tools.

Building your first dashboard

  1. Define the audience and the question, for example "Are our order-to-cash integrations healthy right now?"
  2. Duplicate a predefined page such as Operational Status or Services Status and give the copy a clear name.
  3. Add cards from the card library that answer your question, and remove everything else. Use the Chart Examples page to pick the right chart type.
  4. Review it with the users after their first week and adjust it.

AI-generated dashboards with Joule

With the ALM Dashboard Generation Agent, you no longer need to assemble every card by hand. You describe in natural language what you want to see, and Joule creates graphical dashboard cards from your system and service data in SAP Cloud ALM. The agent is generally available, and SAP estimates that it cuts the effort to create and maintain dashboards by 75%.

Prerequisites:

  • The SAP Business AI feature "ALM Dashboard Generation Agent" must be activated.
  • Joule agents are part of SAP Business AI Premium and consume AI Units.

Example prompts you could try:

  • "Show me the number of open alerts per system for the last 7 days."
  • "Create a card with the status of all integrations of business service Order to Cash."
  • "Show the response time trend of our most used Fiori apps."

Conclusion

The Monitoring Dashboards app turns the many monitoring use cases of SAP Cloud ALM into one view per audience, and with Joule a new card is only one sentence away.

Which dashboards do your operations teams use every day? Share your favorite card or prompt in the comments.
