entry.title: What's new: SAP Best Practices for SAP Integrated Business Planning – Release 2611
entry.content:
This blog post explores the latest updates to SAP Best Practices for SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP), with a particular focus on key improvements and new features in release 2611.

 

New End-to-End Demand Planning Automation Solution Process

We are adding the new solution process IBP Advanced Demand – end-to-end demand planning automation (7M0). It demonstrates how the entire demand planning process can be largely automated while keeping planners involved when critical situations arise. The process combines existing SAP Best Practices processes with new capabilities and is available for the sample planning area I_SAPIBP2.

Overview of the steps of the solution process

This graphic provides an overview of the steps performed throughout the demand planning process. Most steps are automated, so no user involvement is required. Here are some of the new features: 

  • Segmentation forms the foundation of this automated process. Using additional segmentation profiles, we group demand into different clusters. This ensures that each product is assigned to the most suitable algorithm to achieve high forecast quality.
  • Master data rules set different attributes that are used for filtering based on segmentation results.
  • We provide different forecast models for a range of demand patterns. Based on the segmentation and time-series analysis results, the system automatically selects the most suitable model.
  • All steps marked as automated are included in a job template and can be scheduled to run automatically using SAP IBP’s built-in process management.

Overview of alerts delivered with the solution processVarious alerts guide planners to issues that require attention. The new alerts highlighted here help planners address the most critical issues. Of course, planners can still adjust demand plans, for example, based on local market insights. It is also important to understand that the process adapts to changes each time it runs. Each product is reevaluated during every cycle to help maintain high forecast quality. For more information, watch the highlight video.

 

 New solution process IBP Advanced Demand – demand forecast for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition

The next new solution process is IBP Advanced Demand – demand forecast for SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition (7L9). It shows how businesses can use advanced forecasting algorithms in SAP IBP to generate accurate demand forecasts and is now available for the I_SAPIBP2 sample planning area.

The material requirements planning (MRP) run in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition requires forecast data to estimate future demand for materials and components. This information is essential for determining the quantities needed to fulfill customer orders. SAP IBP provides advanced forecasting algorithms and can deliver high-quality forecasts to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition.

Overview of the integration between SAP IBP and SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition

This solution process begins by integrating master and transactional data from SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition, into SAP IBP through SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration. In SAP IBP, the statistical forecasting run generates forecasts that are then transferred back to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition, as planned independent requirements (PIRs). These PIRs serve as input for an MRP run.

 

New solution process IBP Foundation – integration of planned independent requirements to SAP S/4HANA

The final new solution process introduced with SAP IBP release 2611 is IBP Foundation – integration of planned independent requirements to SAP S/4HANA (7M1). It transfers results, such as those from a demand-planning forecast run, to an execution system using SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration as the integration layer. We demonstrate how to configure and deploy this integration flow. After the demand-planning process runs in SAP IBP, the results are read and transferred to the execution system as planned independent requirements. They can then support downstream planning processes, such as an MRP run.

Example of iFlow in SAP Integration Suite, Cloud Integration

 

Sample Instructions for the Exception Management Agent

We published several sample instructions as JSON files for the Exception Management Agent. These agent instructions can be imported directly into the Manage AI Agents app and used as practical examples. They demonstrate how the different instruction items can be structured and how each item guides the Exception Management Agent’s actions. These examples can help you when creating or adapting your own instructions. The files are available for download as a ZIP file in the Training and Education section.

 

Upsize functionality in Transportation Load Building

Another improvement is available in the solution process IBP Advanced Supply – transportation load building (7LV). We added the upsizing functionality, which pulls future transportation demands into a load to make better use of equipment such as trucks. It can add demand until the equipment reaches full capacity. New equipment attributes control this process. As shown in the example screenshot, the truck was loaded until it reached its maximum weight.

Overview of upsizing functionality in Transportation Load Building

 

 

Gating factor key figures in Planner Workspaces

The final improvement I want to highlight is a new workbook in Planner Workspaces for the OBP Supply Planner. This workbook uses gating-factor key figures to show when demand cannot be fulfilled as requested and, through additional key figures, when the issue can be resolved. The solution process IBP Advanced Supply – response planning (7LQ) provides an example.

Overview of gating factor key figures in Planner Workspaces

 

Further Information

Interested in learning more? The following resources offer additional guidance, detailed documentation, and demonstrations of SAP Best Practices for SAP IBP:

  • SAP Signavio Process Navigator – Download all SAP Best Practices assets.
  • Video – Get an overview of SAP Best Practices for SAP IBP in less than three minutes.
  • SAP Best Practices for SAP IBP Blog Series (July 2024) – Explore the fundamentals of SAP Best Practices for SAP IBP in more detail.
  • What’s New Blog for SAP Integrated Business Planning 2611 – Discover further highlights and updates included in the latest release.

Thank you for reading this release highlights blog. Stay tuned for more updates and improvements in future releases.

entry.title: Re: ATP for Production Orders Creation
entry.content:
Hello @Asmaa_KHOULALI 

OPJK configuration defines availability checking rules separately for order creation and order release. Therefore, you can have to different availability scopes during creation and release. That makes sense from business perspective - the ATP scope during creation can be more relaxed (including i.e. purchase orders). The ATP scope during release needs to be more restrictive as you have to make sure you have all the components required.

If you want to have the same ATP response for creation and release, you need to maintain the same availability checking rule for both creation (1) and release (2) in OPJK.

Best regards
